newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bezeq appoints new managing director.
newsitem.headline: Bezeq appoints new managing director.

text.p: Bezeq Israel Telecom's board of directors chose Yoram Turbowicz as its new managing director, a company spokesman said on Monday.
Turbowicz, who has resigned as head of the Industry and Trade Ministry's restrictive business practices division, was unanimously elected as Bezeq's next head. He replaces Yitzhak Kaul.
Turbowicz headed the division, which enforces anti-trust laws, for six years. He is due to leave next month.

The Bezeq appointment, regarded as one of the top management jobs in Israel, was the subject of much press speculation in recent weeks. Among the other candidates rumoured to have been under consideration were Yehoshua Gleitman, Industry Ministry director-general, and Reuven Avi-Tal, managing director of Matav Cable Systems Media Ltd.

Kaul, who has been named managing director of Clal Israel Ltd effective April 1, headed state-owned Bezeq for five years during which the company has been gradually shorn of key segments of its telecommunications monopoly.

The new managing director will be facing new competitive challenges for Bezeq in international calling sometime later this year, after licenses were awarded to two groups in November. By the end of 1998, the government has said it plans to open local and interurban phone service to competition, as well as telecommunications infrastructure.
In addition, the government is expected to make a global offering of Bezeq shares later this year.
